simmer question...

When simmer objects are synchronized and interacting...

patient_traj <- trajectory(name = "patient_trajectory") %>%
  log_(" I'm arriving...") %>%
  seize("doctor", 1)
...
How can doctor read this patient object's list of illnesses and problems 
and  based on that knowledge 
doctor can set the patient object's list of prescriptions and suggestions to patient to change of living habits etc...?
Do I have to write/read to global variable ?

...

thanks for advise,
Kai

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] When simmer objects are synchronized and interacting...
parts:
On Wed, 19 Jun 2019 at 17:02, Kai Lähteenmäki
<kai.j.la...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I mean an object which can "see" both objects properties...
> For instance Desmo-J has that kind of object.
> Desmo-J is slow in some cases, that's why I'm interested in simmer with its C++ backend.
> See their demo pages.
> :
> desmoj.sourceforge.net/tutorial/advanced/waitqueue0.html

Two things:

1. With respect to "object visibility", normal attributes
(set_attribute, get_attribute) are per-arrival. On the other hand,
global attributes (set_global, get_global) are visible by all the
arrivals. Both kinds of attributes are numeric, but they can be used
to set indexes and store info in more complex global R structures when
needed.

2. What you are linking here is not the same kind of use case you
provided in your first email. "Master-slave process cooperation" has
nothing to do with any resource (the "common task" may involve some
resource, but not necessarily). This use case would be equivalent to
batch processing in simmer (see ?batch).

Iñaki
